eam Leadership & Service Excellence

Location: Zuccoli / Darwin, Northern Territory
Employment Type: Full-time
Salary: $67,510 per annum plus superannuation

About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer
We are supporting a care services provider based in Darwin and surrounding areas, operating in the aged care, disability support, and community services sector. The business is known for its commitment to compassionate, respectful, and person-centred care, supporting clients to maintain their dignity, independence, wellbeing, and quality of life. With a growing team and services delivered across multiple client locations, they are seeking to fill the role of Aged or Disabled Carer. This opportunity offers stable employment, meaningful hands-on care work, and the chance to be part of a supportive and inclusive work environment focused on making a positive difference in people’s lives.

About the Role
As an Aged or Disabled Carer, you will provide practical and emotional support to clients who are aged, living with disability, or require assistance with daily activities. The role requires patience, respect, strong communication skills, and a genuine commitment to improving the quality of life of vulnerable clients.

Key Responsibilities
The successful applicant will be responsible for:
- Providing personal care support, including hygiene, grooming, dressing, toileting, and mobility assistance
- Supporting clients with daily living activities in their home and community
- Assisting with meal preparation, feeding support, and basic household tasks
- Supporting clients to attend appointments, social activities, and community participation
- Monitoring client wellbeing and reporting any changes, concerns, incidents, or risks to the supervisor
- Providing companionship and emotional support in a respectful and professional manner
- Following individual care plans, workplace policies, and NDIS-related requirements
- Maintaining accurate records, progress notes, and communication with relevant team members
- Assisting with safe manual handling and mobility support, where required
- Promoting client independence, dignity, choice, and privacy at all times

Selection Criteria
Applicants should be able to demonstrate:
1. Experience providing care or support to aged persons, people with disability, or vulnerable clients
2. A caring, patient, respectful, and reliable approach to client support
3. Good communication skills and ability to follow care instructions
4. Ability to assist with personal care and daily living tasks
5. Understanding of confidentiality, duty of care, and client dignity
6. Ability to work independently and as part of a small care team
7. Flexibility to work across different shifts, including weekends where required
8. Commitment to safe work practices, infection control, and client wellbeing

Required Experience and Qualifications
- Minimum 1–2 years of relevant care/support experience preferred
- Relevant qualification in aged care, disability support, individual support, community services, or similar field is preferred but not mandatory
- Current First Aid and CPR certificate, or willingness to obtain
- NDIS Worker Screening Check, or willingness to obtain
- National Police Check, or willingness to obtain
- Driver licence and access to reliable transport is preferred
- Full working rights in Australia

How to Apply
We are looking for a compassionate, reliable, and safety-minded Aged or Disabled Carer to support clients with daily living activities and help promote their independence, dignity, wellbeing, and quality of life.

To apply, please submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action,
Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a caring and supportive community services business that values compassion, respect, safety, dignity, and person-centred care, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

Applications close: 04 August 2026

Mo's Mobiles is a proudly Australian owned and operated telecommunications retailer and an exclusive partner of Vodafone. Vodafone company has grown to a network of more than 50 stores across the country, helping everyday Australians and small businesses stay connected with the latest smartphones, mobile broadband and NBN devices, and the full range of Vodafone plans. Everything we do comes back to a simple idea: give every customer an exceptional in-store experience and great value on every visit. Our Springfield store, located in the heart of Orion Springfield Central, serves one of South East Queensland's fastest growing communities. We are now looking for a capable and energetic Retail Manager to lead the team and take the store forward.

Key Responsibilities
•	Oversee the day-to-day running of the store from open to close, keeping displays, demonstration devices and point-of-sale material presentation-ready at all times.
•	Build and lead a capable, motivated team by recruiting and inducting new staff, preparing rosters, coaching product knowledge and sales technique, and supervising day-to-day performance.
•	Lead from the shop floor by selling the latest handsets, accessories, mobile broadband, NBN devices and Vodafone plans, matching each customer with the option that best suits their needs and showing them how to set up and get the most from their new device.
•	Set and model the store's customer service standards, and step in to resolve escalated enquiries, warranty and repair bookings and complaints through to a positive outcome.
•	Shape the store's product range and merchandising mix across smartphones, accessories and connectivity devices, and determine the right stock holdings ahead of new releases and peak trading periods.
•	Drive local promotional activity, including in-store campaigns, shopping centre displays and new device launch events, to lift foot traffic and build the Mo's Mobiles name across the Greater Springfield community.
•	Develop and apply the store's buying and promotional plans in line with Vodafone partner guidelines, and review pricing on handsets and accessories so the store stays competitive while protecting margin.
•	Prepare and manage the store budget, set weekly and monthly sales targets, and track results against revenue and cost plans, acting early when performance drifts.
•	Keep accurate records of stock movements and financial transactions, including daily takings, banking and end-of-day reconciliation, and report trading results to head office.
•	Conduct regular stocktakes and manage shrinkage and loss prevention, including the secure handling of high-value devices and SIM stock.
•	Maintain a safe store for staff and customers by applying workplace health and safety requirements, completing routine safety checks and addressing hazards promptly.
•	Follow telecommunications-specific processes with care, including customer identification checks on new connections and the protection of customer information and privacy.
•	Work closely with head office and Vodafone on stock allocations, new device launches and promotional roll-outs, and share local market insights and customer feedback.

Qualifications and Experience
•	A qualification at AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma level (essential).
•	At least one year of relevant experience in a retail environment, ideally in a supervisory or management capacity. Experience in telecommunications or consumer electronics retail will be highly regarded.

Personal Attributes
•	A natural people leader who motivates the team, coaches in the moment and leads by example.
•	Customer-first in outlook, with the patience and warmth to explain technology clearly to customers of every age and comfort level.
•	Results-driven, with sound commercial judgement and a healthy competitive streak.
•	Organised and dependable, with close attention to detail across cash handling, stock and paperwork.
•	A clear and confident communicator with strong interpersonal skills.
•	Curious about technology and quick to master new devices, plans and systems.
•	A high standard of personal integrity, comfortable being accountable for takings and high-value stock.
•	Calm and adaptable during busy trade, new device launches and seasonal peaks.

What We Offer
•	A salary of $75,000 to $85,000 per annum plus superannuation, commensurate with skills and experience.
•	The stability of a permanent, full-time role typically 38 hours per week with an established national retailer.

How to Apply
If you are ready to lead a store where technology meets community, we would love to hear from you. Please apply with your current resume and a short cover letter outlining your retail leadership experience. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

Vehicle Structure & Frame Analysis:
• Conduct comprehensive inspections of vehicle collision damage to assess structural integrity and identify misalignments in frames, unibody structures, and suspension mounting points.
• Utilize advanced frame straightening equipment and hydraulic systems to meticulously pull and correct structural damage back to the manufacturer’s original specifications.
• Diagnose and perform precise repairs on a vehicle's underlying structure, ensuring its safety and performance are fully restored.

Precision Panel Fitting & Alignment:
• Expertly install, align, and fit a wide range of metal panels, frames, and subassemblies—including doors, fenders, quarter panels, and bumpers—to achieve perfect contours and structural integrity.
• Meticulously adjust all replacement parts to ensure consistent, manufacturer-specified gaps and flushness across the entire vehicle body.
• Modify or custom-fabricate replacement body panels through skilled cutting, grinding, bending, and welding of sheet metal to perfectly match the vehicle's original contours.

Technical Interpretation & Mechanical Fitting:
• Interpret complex technical specifications, detailed vehicle blueprints, and comprehensive collision repair guides to determine the correct materials, tools, and sequences for each unique repair task.
• Perform the fitting and installation of mechanical components such as exhaust systems, fuel lines, and associated brackets, ensuring all parts are securely mounted and functionally sound.

Quality Control & Surface Preparation:
• Employ precision measuring instruments including callipers, micrometres, and specialised alignment tools to verify the accuracy of gaps, contours, and dimensions on all repaired or replaced body parts.
• Prepare vehicle surfaces for refinishing by undertaking skilled sanding, application of body fillers, and priming to create a perfectly smooth substrate, ready for painting.
Equipment Operation & Maintenance:
• Configure and operate a range of specialised workshop machinery, including MIG/MAG welding equipment, frame straighteners, and pneumatic/hydraulic tools, tailoring their settings for specific repair applications.

The Ideal Candidate Will Have:
• A proven track record as a Vehicle Fitter, Panel Beater, or in a similar role within the automotive repair industry.
• Formal qualifications in Automotive Body Repair, Metal Fabrication, or a related trade are highly regarded.
• Proficiency in reading and interpreting technical drawings and repair procedures.
• Demonstrated, hands-on experience with welding, metal fabrication, and the use of precision measuring tools.
• Strong mechanical aptitude and a meticulous approach to every task, with an unwavering commitment to quality.
• The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cohesive team in a fast-paced environment.
• A strong commitment to adhering to all workplace health and safety guidelines.

If you are a skilled Fitter ready to take on a rewarding role with a company that values quality and expertise, we encourage you to apply.

A busy and long-standing health-hub in the heart of  Wollongong  is seeking  full-time and part-time General Practitioners . The centre is one of the longest-standing medical centres in the area, with a well-established and diverse patient base, and is located in a  DPA-approved location . 

 The practice is a mixed billing centre with an established reputation for being community-focused. The centre operates Monday to Saturday across two spacious levels, featuring 15 consultation rooms, a fully-equipped treatment room, and a dedicated procedure room. The facilities offer convenient access to a range of on-site allied health services, including X-ray, pathology, physiotherapy, psychology, podiatry, and a specialised Skin Cancer Clinic. Experienced and exceptional nursing support is provided to all GPs, with full-time Chronic Disease Management (CDM) and Health Management nurses. The full-time administration and leadership teams provide support for individual billing choices, assisting GPs in maximising their earning potential and growing their patient base. 

 Practitioners are offered clinical autonomy as independent contractors, along with flexible working arrangements. The practice supports professional growth, including opportunities for GP Registrar supervisors. The practice's partnership with the RACGP simplifies the process of achieving and recording CPD requirements, with free in-house CPD opportunities and discounted registration for industry events. A collegial environment is fostered with support from state-based Medical Directors. Practitioners with special interests in areas such as skin, aesthetics, and occupational medicine are encouraged, with provision and support for these services. 

 The centre is located in Wollongong, a regional city that combines outdoor beauty, cultural charm, and modern amenities. Situated along the Illawarra coastline, the area offers a strong local economy, excellent facilities, and a leading educational institution, the University of Wollongong. Seven Corp on behalf of UON Pty Ltd

Overview:

UON is a Western Australian integrated energy company providing turnkey energy and water solutions to the
mining sector and beyond. Central to this is helping our customers on their decarbonisation journey utilising
the technology, skills and real experience of team members across the business.

UON’s business centres around the design, manufacturing, supply, construction and maintenance of remote,
off-grid power and water infrastructure, with many of the products manufactured in UON’s Malaga facility,
based on proprietary and patented designs.

We are seeking an experienced Purchasing Manager to join our team in Malaga, WA. In this role, you will be
responsible for planning, directing and coordinating procurement and purchasing activities to ensure the
efficient acquisition of materials, products and services required to support business operations. This is a fulltime
ongoing position working 38 hours per week.


Main tasks:

- Determining, implementing and monitoring procurement and purchasing strategies, policies and plans
to support organisational objectives.
- Negotiating and managing supplier contracts to achieve quality, cost and delivery requirements.
- Developing and maintaining supplier relationships to ensure continuity of supply and optimal
commercial outcomes.
- Monitoring procurement activities and purchasing processes to ensure compliance with company
policies and operational requirements.
- Preparing and implementing inventory management plans to maintain required stock levels while
minimising costs.
- Reviewing and monitoring storage and inventory control systems to ensure efficient stock management
and supply availability.
- Overseeing purchasing and inventory recording systems to ensure accurate tracking of materials,
supplies and finished goods.
- Analysing purchasing trends, supplier performance and market conditions to identify opportunities for
cost savings and operational improvements.
- Liaising with internal stakeholders to identify procurement requirements and ensure timely supply of
products and services.
- Coordinating procurement activities associated with transportation, logistics and distribution
requirements.
- Directing and supervising procurement staff, allocating duties and monitoring performance against
established objectives.
- Ensuring purchasing activities support operational efficiency, project requirements and customer
expectations.
- Preparing procurement reports, forecasts, budgets and recommendations for management.
- Performing any additional duties as required from time to time. Perform any additional tasks as
required from time to time.


Required/Relevant Qualifications & Work Experience:

- Bachelor’s degree (or higher qualification) in Supply Chain Management, Business, Commerce,
Procurement, Logistics or a related discipline.
- Alternatively, at least five years of relevant procurement, purchasing or supply chain management
experience may substitute for the formal qualification.


Required/Relevant Skills & Knowledge:

- Strong contract negotiation and supplier relationship management skills
- Demonstrated experience in procurement planning, supplier management, contract negotiation and
inventory control
- Experience working within a medium to large organisation managing procurement functions and
purchasing operations.
- Ability to develop and implement procurement strategies, policies and procedures.
- Sound knowledge of purchasing, inventory management and stock control systems.
- Strong analytical, commercial and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to assess supplier performance and identify cost optimisation opportunities
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Strong leadership and people management capabilities.
- High attention to detail and accuracy
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and procurement management systems
- Ability to build and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.


Annual salary will be between $100,000.00 to $120,000.00 (plus superannuation) depending on level of
experience.
